slides.title: There’s a Lesson in That
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 5 English, Unit 1: There’s a Lesson in That. Unit 1 asks what stories are for. You read “The Camel and the Sparrow”, a fable in which a boastful camel learns that the smallest helper found the water, and “The Silence After the Rumble”, in which Amal sweeps the steps of a courthouse in a town rebuilding after an earthquake. Alongside them you meet twenty-five new words and the adjective and preposition pairs that make feelings precise, such as proud of, anxious about and grateful for. The unit ends with a fable of your own, planned, drafted and revised. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Read a fable closely and state its moral in your own words.
Identify the features of fables and folklore, including animal characters and a stated moral.
Use adjective and preposition pairs accurately in speech and in writing.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to read a fable closely and state its moral in your own words. You will also identify the features of fables and folklore, including animal characters and a stated moral. You will also use adjective and preposition pairs accurately in speech and in writing. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: coal, pouch, encounter, regions, misty, anxiety. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes What Makes a Fable? and Folklore Around the World. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: What Are Adjectives + Prepositions?

slides.narration: The first language focus is What Are Adjectives + Prepositions? An adjective describes a noun or a pronoun by naming a quality, a feeling or an opinion. After a verb, many adjectives cannot stand alone, so they reach forward to a preposition to finish the idea. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Speaking 1: Talk About Stories That Teach
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Talk About Stories That Teach. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
